question: In population-based cohorts, is cerebral small vessel disease (and its MRI markers) associated with the risk of incident dementia and cognitive decline?
eligibility: A population-based or longitudinal cohort of community-dwelling participants.
Exposure is cerebral small vessel disease or an MRI marker of it (white matter hyperintensity, lacunar/silent infarct, cerebral microbleed, vascular brain injury).
Outcome is incident dementia, Alzheimer disease, or cognitive decline/impairment.
A prospective cohort / longitudinal observational study with follow-up.
as_of_source: day after the latest Entrez date among gold records (a lower bound on the review's search date)
source: SYNERGY dataset Bos_2018; 'Cerebral small vessel disease and the risk of dementia' (Alzheimers Dement 2018, doi:10.1016/j.jalz.2018.04.007); gold = label_included==1 rows with DOI via [AID]

naive_blocks.name: Cerebral small vessel disease / MRI markers

notes: Converted from the protocol-first branch. naive_blocks come from protocols written by the fixture author, some tightened while looking at the gold set, so the naive floor may be optimistic.
